questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must carry all three documents in your vehicle when driving.

questions.question: You should never park a vehicle:

options.text: Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Within 30 feet of a flashing signal on the side of a road.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, within 20 feet of a crosswalk, or within 30 feet of a signal light, stop sign, or flashing beacon on the roadway.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and you should slow down.

questions.question: As daylight fades, turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight starts to fade so other drivers can see you. Use high beams only when driving alone on an open road with no other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: In work zones, you should:

options.text: Stay alert, slow down, follow signs and flaggers, and be ready to respond to hazards.
Speed up so you don't slow traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert, slow down, follow signs and flaggers, and be ready to respond to hazards.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and watch traffic carefully. Follow all signs and directions from flaggers. Be prepared to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.explanation: At night, your vision is limited. Always use your headlights. Drive slow enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: Anything that makes you ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: Distractions are anything that makes you take your attention away from driving, take your eyes off the road, or take your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is far from your vehicle.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog crossing, you must stop. Let them cross completely and stay out of your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: If railroad crossing gates are down with flashing warning lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and go when the gates are raised.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and go when the gates are raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop at any railroad crossing with warning signs, lights, or flaggers. Do not drive around lowered gates. It is illegal.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness, like drugs and alcohol, slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The highest safe speed for a residential area.
The highest safe speed for leaving an expressway.
The highest safe speed for entering an expressway.
The highest safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed for leaving an expressway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the highest safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, it shows 30 mph.

questions.question: What is the correct way to do a three-point turn?

options.text: Signal and check your mirrors, then turn.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your left shoulder, and turn only when the road is completely clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your left shoulder, and turn only when the road is completely clear.
questions.explanation: For a three-point turn: Stop near the right edge of the road. Look over your left shoulder for traffic behind you. Signal a left turn. Then complete the turn.

questions.question: When should you always use your signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use your signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, leaving a parking space, entering traffic from an alley, and passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol together?

options.text: You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can make it unsafe to drive. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the person drinking.

questions.explanation: Driving under the influence is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. It puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to avoid accidents.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving right or left.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking an over-the-counter drug and driving?

options.text: Read the label for warnings about driving.
Drive no matter what the label says.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label for warnings about driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect driving. Check the label for warnings. If unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medicine.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What should you do when a school bus stops with its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children are done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus shows its stop signal, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other cars is also dangerous. Other drivers may get impatient and make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: This sign warns you that the road ahead:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a reverse curve. The road will curve to the right, then curve to the left.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes it harder to judge speed and distance. It slows down your decisions and increases crash risk. When tired, you could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage becomes more common. To help prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights and a stop arm when loading or unloading students. You must not move until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: For children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags, the safest place to sit is:

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags help protect adults in crashes, but they can seriously injure children. All children age 12 or under should sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: Approaching a railroad crossing where you do not see or hear a train, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a posted stop sign, a flagger signaling you to stop, or a visible train. If you are not sure if a train is close enough to be unsafe, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety features. For the best protection in a crash, use both your lap and shoulder belts along with the airbags.

questions.question: On a two-lane highway, you approach a stopped school bus with red lights flashing. You:

options.text: May pass if the way is clear.
May pass if someone signals that the way is clear.
May not pass until the bus driver turns off the lights and continues driving.
Must turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not pass until the bus driver turns off the lights and continues driving.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already in the roundabout.
